title: Fusion-guided pruning of an overcomplete Mirror adapter pool
hypothesis: Training an eight-view Mirror adapter pool and pruning by training fusion usage retains target composition better than random four-view pruning while matching a four-view-from-start model at lower actual payload bytes.
physical_object: shared rank-2 input/output factors with eight logical adapter Views and a learned input-conditioned fusion router
mirror_coordinate: one learned Givens angle per logical adapter in the shared rank-2 latent basis
logical_multiplicity: eight trained adapter Views, compacted to four selected Views after fusion training
controls: four-view-from-start models for both full and Mirror parameterizations
teacher: softmax mixture of four active Givens-view adapter functions; four additional pool slots are unused distractor Views

development.selection_metric: held-out normalized MSE; prune top-4 by mean train-set fusion probability only; no fine-tuning after pruning

fresh.run_only_if: all development quality, random-prune and byte gates pass

storage.format: torch.save full and compact model states, indices and metadata

compute.proxy: count active rank-2 adapter projections and router per input before and after pruning

success_gate: Both fresh worlds: usage-pruned Mirror NRMSE2 <=1.10x four-view-from-start Mirror and <=1.10x full overcomplete bank; <=0.50x mean random-prune NRMSE2; compact payload <=0.75x eight-view Mirror.
failure_gate: Any development gate misses; fresh remains sealed.
boundaries: Synthetic teacher with four active functions and four unused views.
Pruned models are not fine-tuned after selection.
No natural task or language claim.
